chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The fasting person anoints himself with perfume and smells the fragrant plant."
ai.seo_question: Does applying perfume or smelling fragrance break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the sensory enjoyment of scent, whether through oil-based perfume (d) or inhaling the fragrance of plants like rosemary (rayhan), does not break the fast. This ruling alleviates concerns regarding the validity of fasts for those who use traditional scents, emphasizing that mere inhalation of aroma without swallowing it is permissible. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that fast-breaking requires the ingestion of substantial matter, not just sensory perception.
